scope: Linux retained-original restoration with preserved copied payload, indexed restart continuation and permission-independent directory pinning
contracts: Pure three-endpoint policy classifies parking, restoration, completion and conflict from exact versions; both staged and finalized copy modes are recognized
RestoreIntent precedes native effects and can be reasserted with exact owner/catalog/checkpoint validation; Restored follows exact native completion and barriers
No-replace parking preserves an unchanged public copy privately before moving original back to absent destination; no payload is deleted
Original restoration requires neither source availability nor a still-existing private copy, but unexpected or duplicate endpoints remain fenced
Each effect revalidates root/manifest and all three endpoints; both endpoints are reconciled after rename errors/success, with root/parent synchronization
Already-complete retries repeat both directory barriers and final Complete verification
Only independently copied directories have staged permissions restored before parking; original permissions are never relaxed to force a move
Linux O_PATH pins owner-unreadable directories for descriptor-relative fchmodat2, with ENOSYS-only fallback through validated procfs descriptor links
Permission fallback validates procfs and exact held/magic-link inode/device; readable synchronization handle opens dot relative to retained pin
Shared copy evidence validation is reused by forward transfer and restoration; native endpoint/phase decisions remain separate
